sections.h2: Where is Ravalli County, Montana, and what is in it?
sections.html:
Ravalli County covers the Bitterroot Valley in western Montana, bordering Missoula County to the north and Idaho to the south and west. The Montana Legislature created it in 1893 from part of Missoula County and named it for Antony Ravalli, an Italian Jesuit priest who came to the valley in 1845.

The Census Bureau puts the county at 2,400 square miles, of which 2,391 are land. U.S. Highway 93 and Montana Highway 38 are the major highways. Large parts of the county are public land, including portions of the Bitterroot and Lolo National Forests and the Lee Metcalf National Wildlife Refuge.

  • City: Hamilton.
  • Towns: Darby, Pinesdale and Stevensville.
  • Census-designated places: Charlos Heights, Conner, Corvallis, Florence, Sula and Victor.
  • Unincorporated communities: Alta, Como, Grantsdale, Medicine Hot Springs and Riverside, among others.

Stevensville's story starts with St. Mary's Mission, founded by the Catholic Church in 1841 and later renamed Fort Owen. The settlement took the name Stevensville in 1864.

sections.h2: How many people and homes are in Ravalli County?
sections.html:
The 2020 census counted 44,174 residents, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 48,582, up about 10 percent.

The county grew from 36,070 people in 2000 to 40,212 in 2010. With 84.4 percent of residents living in rural areas, many Ravalli County sellers are outside the three towns and the one city, so the county treasurer and Department of Revenue matter more than any city office.

sections.h2: What drives the Ravalli County economy?
sections.html:
Agriculture and timber built the local economy, and tourism now supplies more of it. Marcus Daly, one of Butte's copper kings, funded logging in the Bitterroot Valley because Butte's mines needed the lumber.

The valley borders the Selway-Bitterroot Wilderness, and the Lost Trail Powder Mountain ski area sits at Lost Trail Pass on the Idaho border along U.S. 93.

Five K-12 districts serve the county: Corvallis, Darby, Florence-Carlton, Hamilton and Victor. Stevensville is served by its own high school district and by the Stevensville and Lone Rock elementary districts.

sections.h2: Does wildfire risk affect selling a house in Ravalli County?
sections.html:
It can. In a May 2026 release the Bitterroot National Forest said Ravalli County currently has the highest risk to structures from wildfire of any county in Montana. The same release says more than 7,000 homes and structures are at risk in the greater Bitterroot Front project area.

The Forest Service's Bitterroot Front Project covers the front of the mountains along the main valley, from McClain Creek in the north to Trapper Creek in the south, using thinning, harvest and prescribed burning to reduce fuel. The release also notes dense pockets of trees killed by mountain pine beetle, Douglas-fir bark beetle and western spruce budworm.

For sellers near the forest edge, expect buyers to ask about wildfire risk and insurance. A cash sale as is keeps that conversation short, because the buyer takes the house in its present condition.

sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Ravalli County?
sections.html:
Two offices share the work. The Montana Department of Revenue classifies and appraises property, and the Ravalli County Treasurer bills, collects and enforces. Questions about value and class go to the Department of Revenue; questions about payments, receipts and delinquency go to the treasurer.

State law sets two equal payments. According to the Montana Legal Services Association, the first half is due by 5 p.m. on November 30 and the second by 5 p.m. on May 31 of the next year, and a taxpayer may pay the whole year in November.

The 2026 due dates moved in some counties. Gallatin County lists a first half due December 7, 2026, and Yellowstone County lists December 3. Confirm the 2026 date with the Ravalli County Treasurer instead of relying on November 30.

sections.h2: How did Montana's 2026 property tax rates change for Ravalli County homeowners?
sections.html:
For 2026 the Department of Revenue taxes primary residences and long-term rentals on a tiered scale. Each slice of value is taxed at its own rate:

  • 0.76% on the first $378,000 of market value.
  • 0.90% on the portion from $378,001 to $756,000.
  • 1.10% on the portion from $756,001 to $1,511,999.
  • 1.90% on any portion of $1,512,000 or more.

Second homes, short-term rentals such as cabins and vacant residential lots pay a flat 1.90%. Qualified agricultural land is taxed at 2.05%, non-qualified agricultural land at 14.35% and forest land at 0.37%, with a home and one-acre homesite on those parcels taxed at the residential rate if it is a primary residence or long-term rental. To qualify, an owner must live in the home for 7 or more months of 2026, or rent it for 28 or more days for at least 7 months.

That matters at sale. A buyer who plans to use a Ravalli County house as a cabin will face the flat rate, and a bill based on your owner-occupied class may not match what the next owner pays.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Ravalli County property valuation?
sections.html:
Start with the Department of Revenue. File a Request for Informal Classification and Appraisal Review (Form AB-26) within 30 days of the date on your classification and appraisal notice. For the 2025 to 2026 cycle, the valuation date was January 1, 2024, and a late request filed by June 1, 2026 applied to tax year 2026 only.

You can instead appeal straight to the county tax appeal board by filing with the county clerk and recorder within 30 days of the notice date. The board is appointed by the county commissioners and is independent of the Department of Revenue. Further appeals go to the Montana Tax Appeal Board, and from there to district court.

Pay on time while you dispute. Under 15-1-402, MCA, a valid protest requires a written protest filed with the county treasurer and payment of the disputed tax by the due date. Without both, a taxpayer is not eligible for a refund if the value is lowered.

Evidence the Department accepts includes your own estimate of market value on the valuation date, a purchase price within six months of it, a fee appraisal, comparable sales and a builder's cost breakdown.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Ravalli County property tax when you sell?
sections.html:
The tax stays with the property. Montana Legal Services Association explains that delinquent tax becomes a tax lien, the lien attaches at the beginning of August after the unpaid year, and it cannot be released until tax, interest, penalties and costs are paid. The county may keep the lien or sell it to a third party, who receives an assignment certificate.

The owner keeps title for three years after the lien attaches and can redeem by paying the full amount. After that, the lien holder can seek a tax deed, which triggers a public auction. Bids start at the total of all amounts due plus part of the appraised value.

If you owe back tax, a sale lets the title company pay it from proceeds at closing. The deed and a Realty Transfer Certificate are filed with the county clerk and recorder at the same time. Help is available for some owners through the Property Tax Assistance Program for low-income Montanans, the Montana Disabled Veteran program and a land value assistance program for long-held family homes.

faqs.q: When are Ravalli County property taxes due?
faqs.a: State law sets November 30 for the first half and May 31 for the second half, each at 5 p.m. Some counties moved their 2026 first-half dates, so confirm the current date with the Ravalli County Treasurer.

faqs.q: Who sets the value of my Ravalli County home?
faqs.a: The Montana Department of Revenue classifies and appraises property. The county treasurer uses the value on your classification and appraisal notice to calculate your bill.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my valuation?
faqs.a: You have 30 days from the date on your classification and appraisal notice to file Form AB-26 with the Department of Revenue, or to appeal directly to the county tax appeal board through the county clerk and recorder.

faqs.q: What happens if I do not pay on time?
faqs.a: A 2 percent penalty and interest of 5/6 of 1 percent per month are added. Unpaid tax becomes a lien, and after three years the lien can lead to a tax deed and a public auction.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Ravalli County house that has back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The tax lien stays with the property, so it must be paid or settled at closing. A cash buyer can purchase the house as is and pay the balance from the proceeds.
